interest: It details bureaucratic control over occupied Japan's borders. The cases illuminate postwar commercial reopening and humanitarian family dilemmas.
overview: This file documents the regulation and administration of civilian travel, residence, and trade entry into Allied-occupied Japan throughout 1947 under the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP). Governed primarily by SCAP Circular No. 8 and policy paper SWNCC 348, the correspondence illustrates interagency coordination among the Department of State, the War Department, the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and foreign diplomatic missions to manage strict border controls amidst acute domestic food and housing shortages. Key subjects include the rollout of military entry permits (Form DS-513), the gradual resumption of private international commerce regulated by Inter-Allied Trade Board quotas, clearance procedures for foreign missionaries and diplomats, baggage and vehicle import limits, and individual repatriation and family reunification cases.
